narrative.overview:
The dashboard is one dark ring that holds every profile. The ground is Lampblack, a warm near-black, under a slow ambient field of glyphs in Bone at 12%, and text is Bone. Color comes in two layers that never share a form. Apps: an app that has profiles gets one bright hue from a fixed seven-hue palette, and that app's primary action, dots, borders and focus rings carry it, as does its app tile when the app has no installed icon. Sections: each part of the dashboard owns one deep tile color, a rounded square with a Bone glyph, as in macOS System Settings. Apart from those two layers and status, nothing on screen is colored. There is no second hue for an app, no gradient in a hue and no glow. The one exception is the official aidentity logo, which keeps its own blue gradients and glow (The Upstream Logo Rule).

Density is a desktop tool's: a 14px base, 13px labels, a 216px sidebar and 32px gutters. The CLI stays visible: every dialog shows the command it will run, and every Activity entry the command that ran. Surfaces are tonal steps of graphite with 1px borders between them. Depth comes from tone; only things that float (dialogs and toasts) cast a shadow, and the folders on Applications, the one glass object (The Folder Glass Rule).

Motion is brief and springy, and it never overshoots: every surface opens on a click, not a flick, so every spring is critically damped. Controls press to 0.97 on pointer-down and spring back, dialogs rise and scale in from 0.96, panels leave the way they came, pages crossfade, and the sidebar highlight slides to the new page. Hover moves nothing; it changes fill and border (the folders on Applications lean and lift, The Folder Glass Rule). When you open a profile, add one or bring one back, the ground answers once: a ring of denser glyphs spreads from it through the ambient field. With reduced motion on, the springs and both crossfades become static swaps, the ambient field holds one still frame and sends no ring, and every action stays keyboard-reachable. The dashboard is dark-only. The project site (`site/`) is a separate visual world owned upstream, and this file does not describe it.
keyCharacteristics: Warm black ground under a faint drifting glyph field, warm off-white text, graphite steps in between.
One flat hue per app with profiles, assigned once and kept for that app everywhere; apps without profiles stay neutral.
One deep tile color per section, on its sidebar row, its page title and its operation cards.
Flat tonal cards; shadow only on floating layers.
Spring motion with a full reduced-motion path.
Platform UI font only; nothing loads from the network.
The exact `aidentity` command behind every action, shown before and after it runs.

rules.name: The Two Layers Rule
rules.body: A bright hue means an app that has profiles; a deep tile color means a section of the dashboard; Mint, Amber and Negative mean status. Everything else stays on the Lampblack-to-Bone ramp: card surfaces, text, apps without profiles and the counts that are not status. The official logo is the one exception (The Upstream Logo Rule).

rules.name: The Section Rule
rules.body: A page's tiles take its section's color, except a destructive operation's tile, which is Brick. A section color is only ever a tile fill or the current-page highlight, never text, a border or a card surface.

rules.name: The One Running Mark Rule
rules.body: Running is an 8px Mint dot plus "Running" in Mint, on cards, the detail panel, Explore keys and the navigator alike, and the running card or key also keeps its 1px hue border. A closed folder on Applications carries the same mark with its count ("2 running") beside "N profiles". A profile that is not running shows no dot. Under forced colors the dot is drawn in CanvasText.

rules.name: The Flat Hue Rule
rules.body: A hue is a solid fill, a plain dot, a 1px border or a focus ring. Never a gradient, glow, tinted text, tinted background, tinted secondary button or accent stripe, and never a second hue for the same app. The logo's own gradients and glow are its art, not a hue (The Upstream Logo Rule).

rules.name: The Upstream Logo Rule
rules.body: The official aidentity logo is the one sanctioned exception to the Two Layers, Flat Hue and no-site-blue rules. The mark (`assets/logo.svg`) leads the sidebar lockup and the app icon (`assets/icon.svg`) is the favicon, both inline in `index.html` with their own paths, gradients, colors and glow, cropped to the art and scaled, never recolored or redrawn. The logo belongs to the upstream maintainer, and any change to it is a proposal to them.

rules.name: The Own Icon Rule
rules.body: An app is drawn with its own installed icon, read from the app on this Mac, never with artwork shipped in the repo; like the logo, it keeps its own colors, never recolored. The app's hue follows the icon instead: it is the palette hue nearest the icon's own color, so icon and hue read as one, and a neutral icon leaves the pick to the name's hash.

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on an app-colored fill is Lampblack. A badge picks whichever of Lampblack (#060606) and white (#ffffff) contrasts more with its saved color; every preset clears 5.9:1.

rules.name: The System Voice Rule
rules.body: One family: the platform UI font. The dashboard loads no webfonts.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Counts (tab totals, "N profiles" lines, the health summary), the Explore position and every time use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the layer floats above the page (dialogs, toasts). Resting cards and keys never get one, and no hue ever glows; identity and running state are a border or a dot, never height or light. The folders on Applications are the one exception (The Folder Glass Rule).

rules.name: The Folder Glass Rule
rules.body: The folders on Applications are the one glass object in the content layer and the one exception to the shadow rule above and to "hover moves nothing". Each is three layers of in-world material: a back panel of translucent graphite (Raised to Surface at 62–72%), the app's profiles as files (Active to Raised, a Bone hairline on top), and a front panel of smoked glass (Surface to Lampblack, from 8% at the top to 94% at the foot, `blur(16px)`), so the files and the ambient field frost through it, with a soft shadow under the folder and under each file and a neutral Bone sheen at 7% that follows a fine pointer. Nothing is painted for it: no artwork, no second canvas, no color outside the palette; only what is behind the glass shows through. The app's hue keeps its allowed forms: the fallback app tile on the glass (an app without an installed icon), the folder's 1px rim on hover and while open, a file's 1px edge on hover and while it runs in an open folder, and the focus ring. Nothing colored sits under the glass: a closed folder's files, on hover too, show no badge, no running mark and no name (a lifted file is blank paper, never a name cut by the glass's tab); all three appear once it opens and the files clear the glass. What runs still shows while it is closed: the running mark and its count sit on the glass, beside "N profiles", not under it. The label sits where the glass is at least 80% opaque: Muted keeps 5.7:1 there and 4.9:1 under the sheen at its brightest, so neither the glass nor the sheen may get lighter. Under `prefers-reduced-transparency`, `prefers-contrast: more` and forced colors, and without `backdrop-filter`, the glass and the back are solid (the card gradient, Raised to Surface) and the sheen is gone.

rules.name: The Ambient Ground Rule
rules.body: The glyph field is the only thing that moves at rest. It is neutral, every glyph Bone at a flat 12% and never a hue, and it lies under every layer; brightness is glyph density, not ink. It drifts at no more than 30 frames a second, grows denser near the pointer and pauses while the tab is hidden; under reduced motion it holds one still frame, and under increased contrast and forced colors it is gone. It answers four moments, and only these, with one ring of denser glyphs that spreads from where the profile shows and fades as it goes: a profile that starts running (from its Open; 640px over 1.4s), a profile added (from its new card, or its new file on Applications; for the very first profile the ring is wider and crosses to the farthest corner over 3.2s), a profile restored or imported (from the toast that says so), and the dashboard reconnecting (from the connection dot; from Refresh below 768px, where the sidebar is a drawer; the same 640px ring as a profile that starts, since the page coming back is the one recovery nobody pressed a button for). The ring is density only, in the same loop and the same Bone at 12%; Bring to front, Quit and every other action send none. Under reduced motion, increased contrast and forced colors, and in a hidden tab, there is no ring: the running mark, the new card and the toast are the whole feedback. At 12% Muted text keeps 4.6:1 over any glyph; 13% would leave 4.5:1 with no margin, so 12% is the ceiling.

dos: **Do** give each app that has profiles exactly one hue through `--app-color`, and use it only for that app's primary fill, fallback app tile (an app without an installed icon), dots, 1px borders and focus ring.
**Do** define a new hue only as a `--hue-*` token; both scripts read the palette from CSS.
**Do** give a new section a `--tile-*` token and a `.section-<view>` class, and give a destructive operation the Brick tile.
**Do** put Lampblack (#060606) text on any app-colored fill; every hue clears 6.2:1.
**Do** keep text at Muted (#8d8b84) or brighter and at 12px or larger. Muted on Raised (5.4:1) is the lowest text pairing on a surface; over an ambient field glyph Muted is 4.6:1.
**Do** show keyboard focus as a 2px outline in the current accent, offset 4px (swatches use Bone at 3px; controls inside clipping boxes use an inset ring).
**Do** give every spring and crossfade a reduced-motion path that keeps the feedback.
**Do** keep controls at least 36px tall on desktop (swatches 32px) and 44px below 768px.
**Do** show the server's command for every action (Runs line, Activity); never build it in the browser.
**Do** name the primary action Open, or Bring to front when the profile is running, on every surface; Open is always the Secondary (Raised fill, 1px Field border) and Bring to front the hue fill.
**Do** mark running with an 8px Mint dot and Mint "Running", and show no dot when not running.
**Do** default a new badge to the first swatch that is neither the app's hue nor used by that app's other profiles, and ring every badge on a tile in 2px of the surface it sits on.
donts: **Don't** add a light theme. The dashboard is dark-only.
**Don't** bring the site's blue or its light/dark switch into the dashboard. The site is a separate world owned upstream. The official logo's own blue is the one exception.
**Don't** recolor, redraw or animate the logo, cut into its art, or take a color from it; only trim its empty canvas to the art and scale it.
**Don't** put a shadow on a resting card. Shadows belong to dialogs, toasts and the Applications folders (The Folder Glass Rule).
**Don't** use a hue as a gradient, a glow, text color, a tinted background or secondary button, or an accent stripe, and don't add a second hue to an app.
**Don't** give an app with no profiles a hue, and don't use Mint as an app hue; it is status and the default accent.
**Don't** recolor the header Add button; it is always Bone.
**Don't** color anything that is not an app's identity, a section tile, a status or the official logo.
**Don't** use a section color as text, a border, a card fill or a gradient, and don't put Lampblack ink on a section tile.

**Don't** write hex values outside `:root`; use the tokens. The two exceptions are the `dialog::backdrop` scrim, which mirrors `--scrim` because older browsers don't pass custom properties to `::backdrop`, and the official logo in `index.html` (the sidebar mark and the favicon), whose colors are the upstream art's own.
**Don't** load webfonts or any other remote asset.
**Don't** show a secret anywhere, including a command line; masked values read `•••`.
